name: tmp-quit-swallow-negative
description: Negative control: does the harness FAIL a Cmd+Q that did not end the app? It could not before - shutdown_app waited fifteen seconds, sent SIGTERM, logged a line and recorded nothing, so settings-confirm-quit-toggle scored 12 passed, 0 failed on 2026-08-10 while its own log said the chord had been ignored. This stages a page that refuses to unload, clicks into it so the refusal is armed and the page's RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa holds first responder (the swallow needs first responder, not merely a live renderer in the key window), and then asks for a teardown assertion, which is what makes the runner stop the app. The expected result is a red 'quit:shutdown' naming SIGTERM. wip, like every other tmp-* probe: it is built to fail and has no place in the default suite.

actions.note: GATE: the page really loaded off the fixture server. Without it a blank tab would take the quit cleanly and this control would report the opposite of what it measured.
frontmost, so the shutdown step's Cmd+Q reaches Atrium and not whatever else the clean snapshot left in front.

THE PRECONDITION. Chromium suppresses a beforeunload dialog until the frame has sticky user activation, and the click is also what puts the page's RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa in first responder - the same thing the settings window needs before it will swallow anything.
GATE: the page saw the click, so the refusal is armed. The page reports it through document.title, which reaches the run log via TitleWasSet.

assertions.label: the-page-is-armed
assertions.note: Stated again as a graded assertion so the artifact says on its own terms that the premise held.

teardown_assertions.label: the-app-was-signalled
teardown_assertions.note: The app's own account of how it ended, independent of the harness's pgrep bookkeeping. Present here and absent from every clean quit measured on 2026-08-10, which is what lets quit_outcome.py tell the two apart.
